$comment: The hand-written half of the interface A-K coverage map, read by tools/contract-surface.mjs.
Three things live here and nothing else: which contracts a wallet can reach, which app
directory belongs to which interface, and which functions are deliberately outside the app.
Everything else -- the function list, the UI paths, the counts -- is derived from the built
ABIs and the app source, because those two move and a table does not.

aliases.$comment: Hand-written ABI slices in app/src, and the deployed contracts each one addresses. A slice is a real UI path -- useVaultsSummary declares a three-fragment vault ABI because the full one trips TS2589 -- but nothing in the file says which contract it speaks to, so it is said here. One entry is not a slice but another contract's GENERATED binding: the four alignment vaults all implement IAlignmentVault, and useVaultOverview reads the shared selectors (vaultType, accumulatedFees, totalShares) off ANY vault through the endowment family's hooks rather than generating three more bindings for identical selectors. The call is real and the address is the LP vault's, so the credit belongs to the LP vault.

skip.$comment: --- protocol-owner configuration: rare, high-blast-radius, and deliberately not a button in a web build ---

The admin console (interface K) carries the knobs an operator turns in the ordinary course -- rent, decay, agents, curation. Re-pointing a registry, a pool key, a price validator or a treasury is not that: it is a change whose blast radius is the whole protocol, and a UI that can make it is one stolen build artifact away from making it. These are sent from contracts/script with the operator key.
